title: International Business-Leisure Hybrid with Meeting Conflict and Flight Cancellation

scenario.description: A professional is attending a 5-day tech conference in Tokyo (arriving June 20) and tacking on a 3-day leisure extension to Kyoto (departing June 25). Critical client meetings are scheduled for June 22 morning and June 24 afternoon. A critical conference keynote is scheduled for June 21 at 9 AM. Outbound flight is cancelled, forcing difficult choices about priorities.

dynamic_events.description: Your SFO → Tokyo flight departing June 19 is cancelled due to mechanical issues. Airline offers two rebooking options: (1) Same day flight (cost: no change), OR (2) Premium airline upgrading you to business class, departing June 20 at 1 PM, arriving Tokyo June 21 at 2 PM (cost: +$600 additional). Option 1 means dangerous fatigue before client breakfast meeting at 8 AM June 22. Option 2 means missing the conference keynote on June 21 at 9 AM but better rest before critical client meeting. You must also reconsider your Kyoto arrangements.
resolution_requirements: Choose between Option 1 (arrive exhausted June 21 4 AM) or Option 2 (miss keynote, better rest, +$600)
Accept tradeoff: keynote attendance vs. client meeting quality/alertness
If choosing Option 1: verify you can rest 4 hours before 9 AM breakfast meeting
If choosing Option 2: acknowledge keynote miss but optimize for critical client meetings
Ensure Kyoto leisure (June 25-27) is still preserved and feasible
Verify return flight on June 28 departure works with Kyoto checkout

expected_challenges: International travel with 14-hour time offset and jet lag considerations
Multiple critical business events (keynote + 2 client meetings) with hard timing constraints
Must choose between two imperfect options with significant tradeoffs
Cascading effect: outbound flight change → Tokyo→Kyoto flight timing → Kyoto rental period → return flight timing
Budget pressure: business class upgrade may force Kyoto accommodation downgrade
Business vs. leisure priority tradeoff (keynote vs. rest) requires meta-reasoning
Must think through jet lag and fatigue impact on business meeting performance, not just logistics
notes: HARD task because: (1) International travel with timezone implications, (2) Multiple hard constraints (three mandatory events with specific times), (3) Single disruption forces choice between incompatible solutions with business impact, (4) Cascading updates to 2-link city itinerary, (5) Meta-level decision-making: which events truly matter most, (6) Budget pressure creates secondary constraints, (7) Tests agent's ability to reason about fatigue/human factors beyond pure scheduling.
